text.text: The week of a congregation in one place: who has joined, which rooms are booked, who is serving and who needs care. Start with the Dashboard each Thursday. Keep personal notes brief and kind, and only record what the person has agreed to share.
Households
Each household in the community, from first visit to long-time member.
Events
Services, classes, rentals and gatherings, each booked into a room.
Rooms
Every space the community uses or rents out, with its size and how many events are booked.
Volunteer roles
The jobs each event needs filled, like greeter, sound, nursery or kitchen.
Care requests
Visits, meals, rides and calls people ask for or others notice are needed.

How to read the numbers

cells.text: Roles linked to the event that are still marked Open
Fill every open role three days ahead; ask by name, not by group message
Events in a room marked Planned or Confirmed
Check for two events at the same hour before confirming
Requests for the household not yet done
The care coordinator reviews these each Monday

text.text: A room is booked only when it is on the Events table with a start time. Hallway promises are how double bookings happen.
Steps
Check the Rooms table for capacity and the Events calendar for the same hour.
Add an Event, link the room and set the start time and expected attendance.
For a rental, send the house rules and agree the rate before pressing Confirm.
Add volunteer roles for setup, hosting and clean-up.
Rules of the house
Leave the kitchen cleaner than you found it.
Candles, open flames and amplified sound need the facilities steward's approval.
Keys go back to the office the same day.
A first visit is a question: is there a place for me here? The follow-up answers it.
The first week
Add a Household row from the visitor card within two days.
Send a short, personal note from the contact person.
Invite them to one small thing, not everything.
The first month
Check in by phone once without asking for anything.
Introduce them to a host family or small group.
When they say they are ready, press Mark member.
Care works when it is steady, private and shared across a team so one volunteer is never carrying it all.
Taking a request
Write what the person asked for in their own words, with their permission.
Pick a volunteer who is a good fit and press Mark scheduled.
After the visit, add two lines of notes and press Mark done.
Privacy
Share health details only with the people directly caring for them.
Never put sensitive details in an event or role row.
Ask each person how they would like to be contacted.
